claims.text: Dockerfile lines 5-17: FROM sdk:10.0 AS build; WORKDIR /src; COPY global.json, Directory.Packages.props and three .csproj; RUN dotnet restore DonHang.Api/DonHang.Api.csproj; COPY three source folders; RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app --no-restore.
The .NET SDK image contains the compiler and build tools; running an ASP.NET Core app needs only the runtime (aspnet image), which is much smaller than the SDK image.

dotnet restore downloads the packages listed by the projects (versions from Directory.Packages.props with central package management); dotnet publish compiles and writes the files needed to run the app to the output folder; -c Release, -o /app, --no-restore do what the lesson says.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: dotnet restore, dotnet publish, Central Package Management

claims.text: global.json names the SDK version the repository expects (10.0.300, rollForward latestFeature).

With no change, docker compose build api marks all [build 1/11]..[build 11/11] steps CACHED; after appending a blank line to DonHang.Api/Program.cs, steps up to [build 9/11] are CACHED (restore included) and [build 10/11] COPY DonHang.Api/ and [build 11/11] dotnet publish run again.
